instructions: In a medium bowl, stir 4 tbsp of the yogurt with the curry powder, garam masala, the garlic grated or minced, and 2 tsp grated ginger.
Cut the chicken into thin strips. Add them to the bowl with 1/2 tsp of the salt and the pepper and toss until coated. Let it sit for 15 minutes while you do the next steps.
Slice the onion thinly. Shred half the head of lettuce.
In a small bowl, stir the rest of the yogurt with 1 tsp lime juice, the chaat masala and a pinch of the remaining salt. This is your sauce.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add the onion and cook, stirring now and then, for 4 to 5 minutes, until soft with golden edges. Transfer it to a plate.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil to the same skillet. Add the chicken in a single layer, working in two batches if it's crowded. Leave it alone for 2 minutes, until the underside is browned.

Flip the strips and cook the other side for 2 to 3 minutes. You're cooking the chicken to 175°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest piece: it's done when there's no pink left.
Return the onion to the skillet and stir for 30 seconds. Take the skillet off the heat.
Warm the tortillas one at a time in a dry skillet over medium for about 20 seconds per side, or wrap them in a damp towel and microwave for 30 seconds.
Spread about 1/2 tbsp mango chutney over each tortilla. Add some lettuce, then the chicken and onion, then 2 tbsp of the yogurt sauce. Fold in the sides and roll up.
Cut each wrap in half on the diagonal and serve with the rest of the yogurt sauce.
method_notes: Every version has the same shape: spiced chicken, a yogurt sauce, lettuce and onion in a soft wrap. No source had 20 ratings (the best two were 5 stars from 1 vote each), so Liana's Kitchen leads for its simple yogurt marinade and short timing. The sauce (lime and chaat masala in yogurt) is from Go Healthy Ever After; the garam masala marinade, onion and mango chutney are from Irish Heart Foundation. Yogurt is the dish, so the dairy-free tag is dropped. Use leftover cooked tikka chicken if you have it: skip the marinade and the chicken steps and warm it with the onion.
